query: how to hire an intern uk
sub: 6 steps from first idea to first day

steps.title: Define the role
points: Pick one real project they will own
Set 2 or 3 outcomes for the final week
Name a supervisor who has time to mentor
steps.tip: Interns do their best work on real projects, not leftover admin.

steps.title: Get the paperwork right
points: Do a right to work check before day one
Give a written statement of terms from day one
Confirm your employers' liability insurance covers them
steps.tip: Check GOV.UK's guidance on interns before you finalise their terms.

steps.title: Write a clear job ad
points: Lead with the project, not the perks
List dates, hours and location or hybrid
Keep must-have skills to 3 to 5
Add a closing date and how to apply
steps.tip: Use the job title students search for, like "Marketing Intern".

steps.title: Advertise where students look
points: University careers services
Internship job boards
LinkedIn and your own careers page
Student societies linked to the role
steps.tip: Give applicants at least two weeks before the closing date.

steps.title: Shortlist and interview fairly
points: Score CVs against your must-have skills
Ask every candidate the same questions
Use a short task linked to the real work
Reply to everyone, even when it is a no
steps.tip: The same questions for everyone make candidates easier to compare.

steps.title: Onboard and mentor
points: Send a day-one plan before they arrive
Pair them with a buddy in the team
Hold a 15-minute check-in every week
Finish with feedback and a reference
steps.tip: A great internship is the start of your graduate pipeline.

cta_sub: Save this checklist and share it with whoever does your hiring.

captions.linkedin:
How to hire an intern in the UK, in 6 steps.

If you have never hired an intern before, the process can feel unclear. It doesn't need to be:

1. Define the role around one real project
2. Get the paperwork right: right to work check, written terms, insurance
3. Write a clear job ad with dates, hours and location
4. Advertise where students look
5. Shortlist and interview fairly, with the same questions for everyone
6. Onboard and mentor, with a day-one plan and weekly check-ins

Save this for the next time your team plans a hire.
